claims.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the centenary celebrations at Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in Delhi on Saturday evening.
PM Narendra Modi previously spoke at SRCC in February 2013 while serving as the Chief Minister of Gujarat.
PM Narendra Modi recalled his 2013 glass analogy at SRCC, stating that he sees the glass as full, with half water and half air.
PM Narendra Modi cited India's first-quarter GDP growth rate of 7.8 per cent as evidence of economic strength during global uncertainty.
PM Narendra Modi described critics of the GDP growth numbers as 'naraaz fufa-ji' (grumpy uncles) who focus only on negativity.
Congress MP Pawan Khera criticized PM Narendra Modi's speech on X, calling it so boring that 'even onions would burst into tears'.
Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar stated that PM Narendra Modi focused on 2013 and 2047 while failing to address student or public issues.
PM Narendra Modi is currently serving his third consecutive term as Prime Minister and completes 25 years as head of government next month.
PM Narendra Modi stated at SRCC that those who placed India among the 'fragile five' economies are now unable to digest India's 7.8% growth.
Former senior Finance Ministry official Subhash Chandra Garg alleged that the 7.8% Q1 GDP growth rate was overstated due to downward base revisions.
Subhash Chandra Garg claimed nominal GDP growth would have been 2.6 per cent if the previous year's Q1 base had not been revised downward from ₹86 lakh crore to ₹80 lakh crore.
Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan questioned why strong economic growth has not translated into higher private investment and job creation.
India's Ministry of Statistics held a press briefing to defend the revised GDP methodology implemented in February.
PM Narendra Modi stated that if Pakistan indulges in misadventure, Indian armed forces enter their territory and strike.
PM Narendra Modi stated that his Independence Day speech reference to 'Dimagi Naxal' exposed political opponents like a homeopathic dose.
Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar called PM Narendra Modi's address at SRCC a 'PR campaign' held ahead of Delhi University student elections.
PM Narendra Modi criticized the Congress party's student outreach campaign 'Chhatron Ki Goonj', describing it as 'jhooth ki goonj'.
The Congress party's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' campaign focuses on student issues including exam paper leaks, rising education costs, and unemployment.
The Central Government has advanced the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab, and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand to December 1, 2026 – January 4, 2027.
The reference date for the advanced Census enumeration in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab, and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand is set for January 5, 2027.
A 15-day self-enumeration window for Census 2027 will open in the four poll-bound states from November 16 to November 30, 2026.
Assembly elections are scheduled to take place in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa, and Manipur in February-March 2027.
The Census phase in Manipur was deferred following local demands to conduct the National Register of Citizens (NRC) exercise first.
Census 2027 will be India's first digital census and will collect caste data for the first time since 1931.
A revisional round for Census enumeration in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab, and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand will take place from January 5 to January 9, 2027.
Government officials stated dates were advanced to prevent manpower conflicts, as teachers and state personnel are utilized for both census duties and elections.
The Ministry of Home Affairs deferred the Census in Manipur on August 31 amid ongoing state violence and demands for an updated NRC.
The national population census was originally scheduled for 2021 but was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
